literal: Emperor Shenwu, Part One
idiomatic: Emperor Shenwu, Part One

literal: The Grand Ancestor of Qi, Emperor Shenwu, surname Gao, taboo name Huan, style name Heiliuhun, was a native of Tiao in Bohai.
idiomatic: Emperor Shenwu, posthumous temple name Gaozu of Northern Qi, bore the surname Gao; his personal name was Huan and his style Heiliuhun. He came from Tiao in Bohai.

literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Yin served as Administrator of Xuantu under Jin.
idiomatic: In the sixth generation his ancestor Yin had been Administrator of Xuantu under the Jin.

literal: Yin begot Qing; Qing begot Tai; Tai begot Hu — three generations served the Murong house.
idiomatic: Yin fathered Qing, Qing fathered Tai, and Tai fathered Hu; all three generations entered the service of the Murong clan.

literal: When Murong Bao was defeated and the realm fell into chaos, Hu led his followers to submit to Wei and was made Right General.
idiomatic: When Murong Bao suffered defeat and the state collapsed into disorder, Hu brought his band over to the Northern Wei and was appointed Right General.

literal: Hu had four sons; the third, Mi, served Wei, rose to Attending Censor, and for violating the law was exiled to garrison at Huaishuo.
idiomatic: Hu had four sons. The third, Mi, served the Wei court and rose to Attending Censor, but after a legal infraction was banished to live at Huaishuo garrison.

literal: Mi begot the late father Shu, who by nature was frank and unassuming and did not attend to the family occupation.
idiomatic: Mi fathered Gao Huan's father Shu, a man frank and easy in temperament who cared little for the family trade.

literal: He lived south of the White Road; repeatedly there were portents of red light and purple vapor, and neighbors, deeming it strange, urged him to move away to avoid them.
idiomatic: He lived south of the White Road, where red light and purple vapors appeared again and again. The neighbors took this for uncanny and urged him to move elsewhere to escape it.

literal: The late father said: "Who is to say it is not auspicious?
idiomatic: Gao Huan's father replied, "How do you know it is not a blessing?

literal: " He remained there as before.
idiomatic: And he stayed on as before, unperturbed.

literal: When Shenwu was born the late mother Lady Han died, and he was raised in the home of his uterine elder sister's husband, Jing, captain of the garrison prison guard.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan was born his mother Lady Han died, and he was reared in the household of his full elder sister's husband Jing, captain of the garrison prison guard.

literal: As for generations his family had been on the northern frontier, Shenwu was accustomed to its customs and came to be as the Xianbei.
idiomatic: For generations his family had lived on the northern marches, so Gao Huan grew up in frontier ways and lived much like the Xianbei.

literal: When grown he was deep and reserved, possessed of great breadth of mind, lightly regarded wealth and valued men of talent, and was looked to by bold heroes.
idiomatic: As a man he was reserved and far-sighted, generous with money and devoted to worthy companions, and the local men of daring looked to him as their leader.

literal: His eyes had a sharp brilliance; his head was long and cheeks high; his teeth white as jade — in youth he had the countenance of an uncommon man.
idiomatic: His eyes gleamed, his head was long and his cheekbones high, his teeth white as jade; even in youth he wore the bearing of a man marked for greatness.

literal: His family was poor; only when he betrothed Empress Wuming did he first have a horse and was able to serve the garrison as squad chief.
idiomatic: The family was poor, and only after he betrothed Lady Wuming did he acquire a horse and win appointment as squad chief at the garrison.

literal: Duan Chang of Liaoxi, commander of the garrison, often marveled at Shenwu's appearance and said to him: "You possess talent for bringing order and succor; you will not in the end come to nothing.
idiomatic: Duan Chang of Liaoxi, the garrison commander, often admired Gao Huan's looks and told him, "You have the talent to heal the realm; you will not end your days obscurely.

literal: " He thereupon entrusted him with his descendants.
idiomatic: And he entrusted his descendants to Gao Huan's care.

literal: When Shenwu rose high, he posthumously enfeoffed Chang as Minister of Works and promoted his son Ning to employment.
idiomatic: After Gao Huan rose to power he posthumously enfeoffed Duan Chang as Minister of Works and brought his son Ning into office.

literal: Shenwu advanced from squad chief to courier.
idiomatic: Gao Huan moved from squad chief to garrison courier.

literal: Once riding post through Jianxing, clouds and mist darkened the day, thunder followed along, and for half a day it did not cease — as if there were a divine response.
idiomatic: Once while riding post through Jianxing, clouds and mist darkened the day and thunder rolled after him for half a day, as though heaven itself were answering his passage.

literal: Whenever he traveled the roads, there was no look of wind and dust about his coming and going.
idiomatic: Whenever he traveled the roads he seemed untouched by wind and dust.

literal: Again he once dreamed of treading among the stars as he walked; waking, he rejoiced inwardly.
idiomatic: He also dreamed once that he walked treading upon the stars; when he woke he was secretly elated.

literal: For six years as courier, whenever he reached Luoyang he was detailed to the clerk Ma Xiang.
idiomatic: For six years as courier he went each time to Luoyang, where he was assigned to the clerk Ma Xiang.

literal: Xiang once offered meat to Shenwu to eat; Shenwu by nature would not eat standing, and so sat to receive it.
idiomatic: Xiang once fed him meat; Gao Huan, who never ate standing, sat down to accept it.

literal: Xiang took this as disrespect toward himself and had Shenwu flogged forty strokes.
idiomatic: Xiang took this as an insult and had Gao Huan beaten forty strokes.

literal: When he returned from Luoyang, he expended his whole estate to gather clients.
idiomatic: On his return from Luoyang he poured out his fortune to gather followers.

literal: Relatives and friends wondered and asked him; he replied: "When I reached Luoyang, the palace guards of the Feathered Forest together burned the residence of the supreme commander Zhang Yi, and the court feared their disorder and did not inquire.
idiomatic: Kinsmen and friends asked what moved him; he answered, "At Luoyang I saw the Feathered Forest guards burn down the residence of Supreme Commander Zhang Yi in a mob, and the court, fearing worse trouble, never punished them.

literal: When government is like this, how affairs will turn out is plain to see.
idiomatic: When government runs thus, the course of events is already clear.

literal: Can wealth and goods be kept forever?
idiomatic: What good is clinging to property forever?

literal: " From this time he nursed the ambition to cleanse and clarify the realm.
idiomatic: From that day he resolved to set the realm right.

literal: With Sima Ziru, affairs clerk of Yunzhong at Huaishuo, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan he formed a band of comrades ready to run errands; Sun Teng, household clerk at Huaishuo, and Hou Jing, clerk in external military affairs, also joined in friendship.
idiomatic: He made running companions of Sima Ziru, affairs clerk at Huaishuo's Yunzhong desk, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan; Sun Teng, the garrison household clerk, and Hou Jing, clerk for external military affairs, joined their circle as well.

literal: Liu Gui once obtained a white hawk and hunted on the open fields with Shenwu, Jing, Cai Jun, Ziru, Jia Xianzhi, and others.
idiomatic: Liu Gui once came by a white hawk and went hunting on the open steppe with Gao Huan, Jing, Cai Jun, Ziru, Jia Xianzhi, and the rest.

literal: They saw a red hare; each time they closed in it escaped, and they went on as far as Huize Marsh.
idiomatic: They sighted a russet hare that bolted away whenever they closed, and the chase carried them to Huize Marsh.

literal: In the marsh there was a thatched hut; as the hare was about to flee into it, a dog came out from the hut and bit it, and hawk and hare both died.
idiomatic: Near a hut on the marsh the hare was nearly inside when a dog rushed out, tore at it, and killed both hawk and hare.

literal: Shenwu in anger shot it with a whistling arrow and killed the dog.
idiomatic: Gao Huan, furious, killed the dog with a whistling arrow.

literal: Two men came out from the hut and seized Shenwu's robe with great urgency.
idiomatic: Two men burst from the hut and seized Gao Huan's robe in alarm.

literal: Their mother, blind in both eyes, dragged her staff and rebuked her two sons, saying: "Why do you offend the great lord!
idiomatic: Their blind mother, leaning on her staff, scolded them: "Why do you lay hands on our great guest!

literal: " She brought out wine from a jar, cooked sheep, and fed the guests.
idiomatic: She brought wine from a jar, slaughtered a sheep, and feasted them.

literal: She then said herself that she was skilled at reading fortune by touch; she felt over everyone and found them all noble, yet all destinies depended on Shenwu's direction.
idiomatic: Declaring herself skilled in reading fate by touch, she passed her hands over each man and pronounced them all destined for rank, yet said every fortune turned on Gao Huan.

literal: She also said: "Ziru will achieve distinguished rank, but Zhi will not end well.
idiomatic: She added, "Ziru will rise to high office, but Xianzhi will meet an ill end.

literal: " When the meal was done they left; after going several li they turned back to visit again, but where there had been no dwelling at all — those before had not been human.
idiomatic: After the meal they rode on, but a few li later turned back to find the place, and there was no hut at all—their hosts had not been of this world.

literal: From this the company all the more revered and marvelled at him.
idiomatic: From that day his companions held him in still greater awe.

literal: In the first year of Xiaochang, Du Luozhou of Rouxuan garrison rebelled at Shanggu, and Shenwu with his like-minded comrades followed him.
idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaochang (525), Du Luozhou of Rouxuan garrison rebelled at Shanggu, and Gao Huan and his companions joined him.

literal: He loathed Luozhou's conduct and secretly with Jing, Duan Rong, and Cai Jun plotted against him.
idiomatic: Disgusted by Luozhou's methods, he secretly plotted with Jing, Duan Rong, and Cai Jun.

literal: The plot did not succeed and he fled; Luozhou's cavalry pursued him.
idiomatic: The plot failed and he fled, with Luozhou's horsemen in pursuit.

literal: Wenxiang and the Empress Dowager of Yongxi of Wei were both young; Empress Wuming on the ox bore them in her arms.
idiomatic: Wenxiang and the future Empress Yongxi of Wei were still small children; Empress Wuming carried them on the ox in her arms.

literal: Wenxiang repeatedly fell from the ox; Shenwu bent his bow intending to shoot him to settle whether to go on.
idiomatic: Wenxiang kept falling from the ox; Gao Huan strung his bow as if to shoot the boy dead and be rid of the burden.

literal: The empress called to Rong for rescue; thanks to Rong quickly descending to take him up, he was spared.
idiomatic: Empress Wuming cried to Duan Rong for help, and Rong leapt down in time to catch the boy and save him.

literal: He then fled to Ge Rong, and again broke away and returned to Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.
idiomatic: He fled next to Ge Rong, then broke away again and took refuge with Erzhu Rong at Xiurong.

literal: Earlier Liu Gui had served Rong and lavishly praised Shenwu's excellence; only now did he first gain an audience, but because he was haggard, Rong did not regard him as extraordinary.
idiomatic: Liu Gui had long served Erzhu Rong and spoken lavishly of Gao Huan's gifts; now Gao Huan finally met Rong face to face, but worn and haggard as he was, Rong saw nothing remarkable in him.

literal: Gui then changed Shenwu's clothing and sought another audience.
idiomatic: Liu Gui dressed Gao Huan in fresh clothes and arranged another meeting.

literal: Thereupon he followed Rong to the stables.
idiomatic: He then followed Rong into the stables.

literal: In the stable there was a vicious horse; Rong ordered its mane clipped.
idiomatic: A vicious stallion was in the stable, and Rong ordered its mane clipped.

literal: Shenwu then clipped it without adding halter or tie, and in the end it did not kick or bite; when done he rose and said: "Handling wicked men is also like this horse.
idiomatic: Gao Huan clipped it without halter or hobble, and the beast never kicked or bit; when he finished he stood and said, "Taming wicked men is like taming this horse.

literal: " Rong thereupon seated Shenwu below his couch, dismissed those on either side, and inquired about current affairs.
idiomatic: Rong then seated Gao Huan below his couch, dismissed his attendants, and questioned him on the state of the realm.

literal: Shenwu said: "I hear you have horses in twelve valleys, grouped by color — to what end do you keep them all?
idiomatic: Gao Huan asked, "I hear you pasture horses in twelve valleys, sorted by color—what do you mean to do with them?

literal: " Rong said: "Just speak your mind.
idiomatic: Rong replied, "Tell me what you have in mind.

literal: " Shenwu said: "At present the Son of Heaven is foolish and weak, the Empress Dowager debauched and disorderly, favorite minions hold command at will, and court governance does not function.
idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "The emperor is weak and the empress dowager debauched; favored creatures command at will and the court has ceased to govern.

literal: With your heroic martial power, sir, if you seize the moment and strike, punish Zheng Yan and Xu He and cleanse the emperor's side — hegemony can be achieved at a flick of the whip.
idiomatic: With your might, my lord, rise now, strike down Zheng Yan and Xu He, cleanse the emperor's side—and dominion over the realm is yours at a flick of the whip.

literal: This is Heiliuhun's intent.
idiomatic: That is Heiliuhun's counsel.

literal: " Rong was greatly pleased; they spoke from midday until midnight before he departed.
idiomatic: Rong was delighted; they talked from noon until midnight before Gao Huan left.

literal: From this time he took part in every military council.
idiomatic: From then on Gao Huan was included in every council of war.

literal: Later following Rong he moved to hold Bing Province, arrived at Pang Cangying of Yangzhou township, and lodged in a round walled compound.
idiomatic: Later, when Rong shifted his base to Bing Province, Gao Huan stayed with Pang Cangying of Yangzhou township in a round-walled compound called Tuanjiao.

literal: Whenever he returned from outside, the host from afar heard his footsteps shaking the ground.
idiomatic: Whenever Gao Huan returned from outside, his host heard from far off footsteps that seemed to shake the earth.

literal: Cangying's mother often saw over the compound a red vapor blazing up to the sky.
idiomatic: Cangying's mother often saw over the compound a scarlet aura blazing up to heaven.

literal: Again Cangying once at night wished to enter; a man in blue robes drew a sword and shouted: "Why do you offend the king!
idiomatic: One night Cangying tried to enter and a man in blue robes drew a sword and cried, "How dare you disturb the king!

literal: " When the words ended he was not to be seen.
idiomatic: When he finished speaking, the figure vanished.

literal: At first taking it for strange, he secretly watched and saw only a red serpent coiled on the bed; he was all the more startled and marveled.
idiomatic: At first puzzled, he stole a look inside and saw only a red serpent coiled on the bed; his wonder only grew.

literal: Thereupon he slaughtered an ox and divided the meat, generously presenting it to him.
idiomatic: He slaughtered an ox and brought Gao Huan generous gifts of meat.

literal: Cangying's mother asked to take Shenwu as an adopted son.
idiomatic: Cangying's mother asked to adopt Gao Huan as a son.

literal: When he achieved his ambition he made that dwelling his mansion, called the Southern Residence.
idiomatic: After Gao Huan rose to power he made the house his own mansion and called it the Southern Residence.

literal: Although gateways and lanes were broadened and halls lofty and splendid, the original Tuanjiao where he had lived he plastered with stone and lime, preserving it undestroyed; by the time of Emperor Wenxuan it became a palace.
idiomatic: Though his new halls grew wide and grand, he left the original Tuanjiao compound plastered in whitewashed stone, never torn down; under Emperor Wenxuan it became a palace.

literal: Shortly thereafter Rong made Shenwu trusted commander.
idiomatic: Soon after, Erzhu Rong appointed Gao Huan trusted commander.

literal: At this time Wei Emperor Ming bore hatred for Zheng Yan and Xu He, who pressed the Empress Dowager Ling; he dared not restrain them and secretly sent Rong to raise troops inward.
idiomatic: At that time Emperor Ming of Northern Wei loathed Zheng Yan and Xu He, who dominated Empress Dowager Ling, but dared not move against them openly; he secretly urged Erzhu Rong to march on the capital.

literal: Rong made Shenwu vanguard.
idiomatic: Rong made Gao Huan his vanguard.

literal: Reaching Shangdang, Ming again privately ordered him to halt.
idiomatic: When the army reached Shangdang, the emperor secretly ordered a halt.

literal: When the emperor suddenly died, Rong then entered Luoyang and intended to usurp the throne.
idiomatic: When the emperor died suddenly, Rong entered Luoyang and prepared to seize the throne himself.

literal: Shenwu remonstrated; fearing he would not listen, he asked to cast an image and divined by it; the casting did not succeed, and so Rong stopped.
idiomatic: Gao Huan remonstrated; fearing Rong would not heed him, he had a Buddha image cast for divination—and when the casting failed, Rong abandoned the plan.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang was enthroned, for merit in settling the plan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Tongdi.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang took the throne, Gao Huan was enfeoffed Baron of Tongdi for his role in the settlement.

literal: When Erzhu Rong attacked Ge Rong, he had Shenwu persuade seven bandit chiefs styling themselves kings to submit.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong campaigned against Ge Rong, he sent Gao Huan to talk seven rebel kings into surrender.

literal: Later with Mobile Headquarters Yu Hui he defeated Yang Kan at Mount Tai; soon with Yuan Tianmu he defeated Xing Gao at Jinan.
idiomatic: He later joined Mobile Headquarters Commander Yu Hui to defeat Yang Kan at Mount Tai, and soon after joined Yuan Tianmu to crush Xing Gao at Jinan.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to chief of the third garrison populations and was constantly within Rong's tent.
idiomatic: He rose to become chief of the third garrison peoples and remained constantly at Erzhu Rong's side.

literal: Rong once asked those beside him: "One day without me — who could command the army?
idiomatic: Rong once asked his companions, "If I were gone, who could lead these armies?

literal: " All named Erzhu Zhao.
idiomatic: All named Erzhu Zhao.

literal: He said: "This one can just lead three thousand cavalry back; the man fit to replace me in commanding the masses is only Heiliuhun.
idiomatic: Rong said, "Zhao can lead three thousand horsemen home, but only Heiliuhun is fit to replace me in command of the host.

literal: He thereupon warned Zhao: "You are not his match; in the end you will be bridled by him.
idiomatic: He warned Zhao, "You are no match for him; in the end he will put the ring in your nose.

literal: " He then made Shenwu Inspector of Jin Province.
idiomatic: He thereupon appointed Gao Huan inspector of Jin Province.

literal: Thereupon he greatly gathered riches; through Liu Gui he bribed Rong's key men and came fully to know their intentions.
idiomatic: Gao Huan amassed wealth on a grand scale and, through Liu Gui, bought off Erzhu Rong's inner circle until he knew their minds completely.

literal: At the time the horn of the provincial storehouse spontaneously sounded without cause; Shenwu took it as strange; before long Xiaozhuang executed Rong.
idiomatic: About then a horn in the provincial storehouse sounded of its own accord; Gao Huan took it for an omen—and soon Emperor Xiaozhuang killed Erzhu Rong.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao from Jinyang was about to raise troops and march to Luoyang, he summoned Shenwu.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao prepared to march from Jinyang on Luoyang, he summoned Gao Huan.

literal: Shenwu sent chief clerk Sun Teng to decline, citing that Jiang-Shu and Fen-Hu wished to rebel and he could not leave his post.
idiomatic: Gao Huan sent his chief clerk Sun Teng to excuse him, claiming the Jiang-Shu and Fen-Hu tribes were on the verge of revolt and he could not abandon his post.

literal: Zhao bore resentment.
idiomatic: Zhao resented the refusal.

literal: Teng reported back; Shenwu said: "Zhao raises troops against his sovereign — this is a great rebel; I cannot serve him long.
idiomatic: When Sun Teng returned, Gao Huan said, "Zhao is marching against the throne—he is a traitor, and I cannot serve him much longer.

literal: " From this time he first formed a plan against Zhao.
idiomatic: From that moment he began plotting against Erzhu Zhao.

literal: When Zhao entered Luoyang and took Emperor Zhuang north as prisoner, Shenwu heard and was greatly alarmed.
idiomatic: When Zhao entered Luoyang and dragged Emperor Xiaozhuang north as a prisoner, Gao Huan was dismayed.

literal: Again he sent Sun Teng to feign congratulations to Zhao, and thereby secretly spy out where Xiaozhuang was, intending to seize him and raise a righteous army — it did not succeed.
idiomatic: He sent Sun Teng to offer Zhao false congratulations while secretly seeking Emperor Xiaozhuang's whereabouts, intending to rescue him and raise the banner of revolt—but the plan failed.

literal: He then wrote advising Zhao, saying it was not fitting to hold the Son of Heaven and thereby incur evil reputation throughout the realm.
idiomatic: He wrote urging Zhao that holding the emperor captive would earn him infamy throughout the realm.

literal: Zhao did not accept; he killed the emperor, and with Erzhu Shilong and others enthroned Prince Changguang Ye and changed the era name to Jianming.
idiomatic: Zhao refused heed, killed the emperor, and with Erzhu Shilong and others enthroned Prince Changguang of Changguang, changing the era name to Jianming.

literal: Shenwu was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyang Commandery.
idiomatic: Gao Huan was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyang Commandery.

literal: When the Feiyetou tribe Helouling Bofan entered Xiurong and pressed Jinyang, Zhao summoned Shenwu.
idiomatic: When Helouling Bofan of the Feiyetou entered Xiurong and threatened Jinyang, Zhao again summoned Gao Huan.
